title: The Age photos of the week, June 27, 2026
text:
The week in photos from our award-winning staff photographers and regular contributors at The Age.

June 27, 2026 — 1:28pm

1/24

Australia's newest sprint star, Eddie Nketia, recently broke the national 100m record in a wind-assisted race.Credit:Justin McManus

2/24

The Discovering the Impressionists exhibition at Geelong Gallery.Credit:Ruby Alexander

3/24

Uncle Vince Kirby pictured among the massive gum trees.Credit:Jason South

4/24

Australian Ballet's first rehearsal of Copland Dance Episodes.Credit:Simon Schluter

5/24

Keira Hannigan and her daughter, Annabelle Holland, 5. Annabelle has a rare genetic disorder called ReNU syndrome.Credit:Jason South

6/24

Rose Hotel owner Neil Spark with his dog Bailey. City of Yarra attempted to fine Spark over having dogs in his pub.Credit:Justin McManus

7/24

Clare Taheri, with her children Persephone and Theodore, navigates childcare options.Credit:Eddie Jim

8/24

Brendan Trew, 47, had a heart attack earlier this year, and benefited from a rehab program. It helped rebuild his strength and taught him about his heart, diet and exercise.Credit:Chris Hopkins

9/24

Emma Whiting, Flawless Flowers owner, at Acland Court Shopping Centre.Credit:Eddie Jim

10/24

Architect Danielle Peck through the peephole of one of the doors of the Sunbury Community Arts and Cultural Building, a former asylum. Credit:Jason South

11/24

Former Socceroo Thomas Deng at the Immigration Museum’s new show Football Is Home.Credit:Joe Armao

12/24

Harry Townsend frequently cycles along Chapel Street, which is one of the worst places for bike crashes in Melbourne.Credit:Eddie Jim

13/24

Tamara Tesseyman says it has been difficult accessing support from the TAC since she and her son were injured in a road crash.Credit:Eddie Jim

14/24

Environment Victoria chief executive Jono La Nauze.Credit:Jason South

15/24

Shark researcher Kent Stannard shares his knowledge on how to avoid sharks and what to do if you encounter one.Credit:Ruby Alexander

16/24

Friends of Nyah-Vinifera Park was set up in 1996 to protect the beautiful red gum and black box floodplain forests of Nyah-Vinifera from logging.Credit:Jason South

17/24

Port Melbourne Primary School students before Australia's World Cup match with Paraguay.Credit:Justin McManus

18/24

Fans gathered before dawn at Federation Square to watch Australia take on the United States in the World Cup.Credit:Joe Armao

19/24

Members of the Australian Education Union’s branch council celebrate members’ rejection of the government’s pay offer.Credit:Joe Armao

20/24

The opening day of the impressionists exhibition at Geelong Gallery.Credit:Ruby Alexander
